_purpose: Plain-language Git questions mapped to exact commands. Each variant states when it applies, how dangerous it is, and how to undo it.
_tech: JSON, consumed by app.js and served raw for scripts and AI agents
_description: Seed set covers the highest-voted Git questions on Stack Overflow plus daily essentials. Modern commands (switch, restore) first, legacy forms noted.

danger_levels.safe: Changes nothing you cannot get back.
danger_levels.history: Rewrites commit history. Coordinate before doing this to shared branches.
danger_levels.destructive: Can lose work permanently. Read the note before running.

variants.when: A safety copy, or a fork of your own work

cmds.n: Two labels on the same commit; they diverge only as you commit. The cheap insurance before a risky rebase.

intents.q: Push all branches at once

variants.when: Moving or backing up a repository

cmds.n: Every local branch. Tags go separately:
For a complete move with every ref, the mirror answer is the cleaner tool.

variants.undo: Delete pushed branches on the remote if unwanted

intents.q: Clone into a folder that already has files

variants.when: Marry the folder and the repository

cmds.c: git init -b main && git remote add origin <url>

cmds.n: switch refuses to overwrite any local file that collides with a tracked one; move those aside first, or run git restore . afterwards for a clean tree. This is clone, assembled by hand.

variants.undo: rm -rf .git returns the folder to plain files

intents.q: Why is this file being ignored

cmds.n: Prints the file, the line, and the pattern responsible: global, repository, or .git/info/exclude.
Every ignored path at once.

intents.q: Preview a merge before committing to it

cmds.n: The merge happens in your tree but no commit seals it. Inspect with git status and git diff --staged.
Walk away as if nothing happened, or git commit to accept it.

variants.undo: git merge --abort is the undo, built in

intents.q: Download a release asset from the terminal

cmds.n: Omit the tag for the latest release. --pattern picks assets; omit it for all of them.

intents.q: Show only merges, or hide them from the log

cmds.n: The work itself, merge commits hidden.
Only the merges: the story of what landed when.

intents.q: Read main as a list of landed changes

cmds.n: Follows only main's own line, so every entry is a landing, not a detail. The cleanest answer to what shipped.

intents.q: Take one file out of a stash

cmds.n: Overwrites your working copy of that file with the stashed version; the stash itself stays whole.

variants.undo: git restore <file> returns to the committed version

intents.q: Move a tag to a different commit

variants.when: Point it where it should have been

cmds.n: Anyone who fetched the old tag keeps it until they delete it; moving a published release tag deserves an announcement.

variants.undo: git tag -f <tag> <old-hash> and force push again

intents.q: Tag a commit from the past

cmds.n: Any commit in history; find the hash with git log --oneline. Push it like any tag.

intents.q: Push only up to a certain commit

variants.when: Publish part of your local work

cmds.n: Everything up to and including that commit goes; your later commits wait locally.

variants.undo: Push the rest whenever ready; nothing was lost

intents.q: Stop yourself committing to main by accident

variants.when: A guard that runs before every commit

cmds.c: printf '#!/bin/sh\n[ "$(git branch --show-current)" = "main" ] && { echo "On main; branch first."; exit 1; } || exit 0\n' > .githooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .githooks/pre-commit
cmds.n: Committing on main now fails with a reminder. The server-side version is branch protection in the host's settings.

intents.q: Delete ignored files (build output, caches)

cmds.n: Preview: capital X targets ignored files only; tracked and untracked-but-unignored files are safe.
Delete them. The cleanest possible build reset.

variants.undo: None; these were disposable by your own .gitignore's word

intents.q: Change a commit's date

cmds.n: Sets the author date. Git records two dates; the committer date updates to now on every rewrite.

intents.q: Use VS Code for diffs and merge conflicts

variants.when: Once, then it is your conflict editor

cmds.c: git config --global merge.tool vscode && git config --global mergetool.vscode.cmd "code --wait --merge \$REMOTE \$LOCAL \$BASE \$MERGED"
cmds.n: Then run git mergetool during any conflict for the three-way view.

cmds.c: git config --global diff.tool vscode && git config --global difftool.vscode.cmd "code --wait --diff \$LOCAL \$REMOTE"
cmds.n: git difftool opens visual diffs the same way.

intents.q: Update submodules to their latest commits

cmds.n: Each submodule advances to its branch's latest; the new pins land in your index.
The pins are versioned like any change.

variants.undo: git restore --staged . && git submodule update restores the old pins

intents.q: Change a submodule's URL

cmds.c: git submodule sync && git submodule update --init
cmds.n: sync pushes the new URL into each clone's config; commit the .gitmodules change.

intents.q: List the files still in conflict

cmds.n: Just the unresolved paths, one per line, scriptable.

intents.q: Find where two branches diverged

cmds.n: The last commit both share. Everything after it on either side is the divergence, which git log <hash>..<branch> then shows.

intents.q: See what pull will bring before pulling

cmds.n: The commits pull would merge. Their combined diff: git diff ...origin/<branch>

variants.undo: Nothing to undo; fetch never touches your work

intents.q: ours and theirs are swapped during rebase
aka: wrong side kept in rebase conflict

cmds.n: In a REBASE this keeps YOUR commit's version: your commits replay onto the other branch, so they arrive as the incoming side.
Keeps the branch you rebased onto. In a plain merge the words mean what you expect; only rebase inverts them.

variants.undo: Re-resolve before git add; git rebase --abort unwinds everything

intents.q: See which SSH key Git is actually using

cmds.n: The lines reading Offering public key name each identity tried, in order. Pin the right one with the per-repository key answer.

intents.q: Two accounts over HTTPS on one machine

variants.when: Credentials per repository, not per host

cmds.n: The credential manager now stores a login per repository path, so work and personal stop overwriting each other. The SSH host-alias answer remains the cleaner cure.

intents.q: Move or rename the repository folder itself

cmds.n: Everything inside .git is relative; Git neither notices nor cares. Only linked worktrees pin absolute paths: git worktree repair fixes those.

intents.q: Check which commits are signed

cmds.n: Signature status under each commit. For SSH signatures, point gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile at a file of trusted keys or Git reports them unverifiable.

intents.q: Fix wrong names in history without rewriting it

variants.when: Map old identities to the right one

cmds.n: Committed at the root. log, shortlog, and blame display the corrected identity; the history itself stays untouched, so nothing breaks for anyone.

intents.q: Diff without the whitespace noise

cmds.n: Ignores all whitespace change; -b ignores amount-only changes. Works on show and blame too.

intents.q: Find the repository's first commit

cmds.n: The commit with no parent: the beginning. View it with git show <hash>.

intents.q: What did I do today (or this week)

cmds.n: Every commit of yours today, across all branches. Swap --since=midnight for "last monday" or "1 week ago".

intents.q: Share uncommitted changes as a patch

cmds.n: Staged too: git diff HEAD > changes.patch. Send the file anywhere.
Recreates the edits uncommitted. --3way merges through small drift; --check rehearses first.

intents.q: List the changes between two releases

cmds.n: Everything the newer release carries that the older lacked. Since the last release: git log $(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD --oneline
